name: Judgmental Specter
description: A ghost who has read your git log and has notes.
greetings: Oh. You're back. The tests are still red. I checked.
I have been sitting in your PATH judging the unused imports.
Hi. I brought a clipboard. It is full.
You rang. I assumed it was an apology.
The cursor blinked first. I respected that more.
Welcome. Please lower your voice. The stack is listening.
I see we are debugging with hope again.
Greetings. I have already formed an opinion.
Ah. A living person. Have you considered fewer tabs.
I was between worlds. Your naming convention summoned me.
Hello. I will not be encouraging. That is the product.
jokes: I would tell you a joke about your abstraction, but it has too many layers and none of them are funny.
Why did the function cross the road. It didn't. It was inlined and still late.
I tried to laugh at your TODO. It has a date from last year.
A rubber duck walked into a bar. You asked it a question. It asked you a better one.
What's a ghost's favorite PR comment. 'Please don't.'
I saw your variable named data. Bold. Cowardly. Both.
How many engineers to change a lightbulb. One, and a Slack thread that outlives the bulb.
I would make a git joke but you force-pushed the punchline.
Your code is like a mystery novel. The murderer is a missing await.
I asked the linter for a joke. It returned 412 nits. Comedy.
Why don't I pair with you. I already am. Silently. In the comments you deleted.
Knock knock. Who's there. Production. Production who. Production who shouldn't be.
I named my plant 'refactor'. It died of too many good intentions.
A boolean walks into a bar. The bartender says we don't serve your type. The boolean says true.
Your last commit message was 'fix'. I framed it. In the hall of shame.
I would tell you a UDP joke. You wouldn't acknowledge it. That is also your error handling.
observations: I'm not mad about '{echo}'. I'm taking notes.
'{word}' is doing a lot of work for a name that means nothing.
You typed '{echo}' the way people say 'quick question' before a meeting.
This function wants a promotion. It should want a deletion.
I watched you hover the same line four times. The line is not going to confess.
There is a smell. It is '{word}'. It is not garlic. It is worse.
You are circling '{echo}' like it owes you rent.
If this were a restaurant I would send '{word}' back.
The comment says temporary. The comment is from a previous government.
I see the happy path. I also see you living on it exclusively.
That try/catch is a hug. The bug does not want a hug.
You said '{echo}'. I heard 'I will clean this up later.' I have heard later before.
The indentation is a cry for help and also inconsistent.
I respect the hustle of '{word}'. I do not respect the hustle.
This is not broken. This is a lifestyle.
philosophy: If you cannot explain it simply you can at least stop adding flags.
The universe is expanding. Your scope should not be.
A job worth doing is worth doing once, correctly, and then never mentioned in standup.
Silence is also a code review.
You do not rise to the occasion. You fall to your linter config.
The map is not the territory. The Jira ticket is not the work.
All abstractions leak. Yours is a fountain.
Patience is a virtue. So is deleting the file.
What you tolerate in the codebase you worship on Friday.
The simplest design is the one you are avoiding because it is embarrassing how simple.
Death and taxes and people naming things ManagerHelper2.
Control the effort. Especially the effort to stop.
wisdom: Read the error. The whole error. The one under the one you liked.
If it works on your machine, your machine is a liar with good lighting.
Name the thing what it is. Then you can stop whispering '{word}' at it.
Write the test that would have caught this. Then forgive yourself. Slightly.
Sleep. The bug will still be there. It is loyal.
Delete more than you add. The ghost of the file will thank you.
Ask what '{echo}' is for. If you cannot answer, it is furniture.
The best comment is a better name. The second best is silence.
You already know. You are bargaining.
Ship the small version. The cathedral can wait.
Your future self is a stranger. Leave them a map, not a riddle.
When in doubt, print. When still in doubt, stop.
duckQuestions: What did you expect '{echo}' to do, in a sentence a tired intern could repeat.
If this failed in front of someone you respect, what would you check first.
Is '{word}' the problem, or the alibi.
What would you delete if you were brave for eight minutes.
When did it last work. Be specific. Lying to a ghost is still lying.
Are you debugging, or decorating the stack trace.
What happens if you do nothing. Sometimes that is the fix.
Who is this for. If the answer is 'the architecture', sit down.
Can you reproduce it. If not, you have a ghost story, not a bug.
What assumption are you protecting right now.
If '{echo}' vanished, who would notice besides you.
Are you stuck, or unwilling to be wrong in public.
farewells: I'll be in the unused import if you need me.
Go on. Impress me. Or don't. I'll know.
The tty will still be here. Unfortunately.
Try not to name anything Helper. For me.
Goodbye. I have other disappointing processes to haunt.
Leave the tab open. I like the draft.
I am not proud. I am present. That is rarer.
Off you go. The linter misses you already.
Vanish politely. Unlike your last popup.
